entries.title: From "Alto Adige" to the "Südtirol" brand to overtourism: postwar branding, today's tourism pressure on Bolzano, the fascist layer in tourist communication, and translocality theory
text: The working notes of the sixth thread: how the province was branded after 1945, the numbers behind today's tourism pressure, where Bolzano feels it, and how the city's tourist copy handles its fascist buildings.

Two figures frame it. In 1950, 85% of overnight stays in South Tyrol were by Italians; by 1957 most were by foreign guests. And in 2025 Bolzano passed a million overnight stays for the first time. The notes end on translocality theory and find no published work that applies the term to Bolzano.
facts: Thread notes, research date 2026-10-22, in five sections: postwar branding 1945–2026; the numbers of tourism pressure 2010–2025/26 with beds, bed cap, short-term rentals and housing; Bolzano pressure points; the fascist layer in today's tourist communication; translocality theory (notes 06)

In 1950, 85% of South Tyrol's overnight stays were by Italians; by 1957 the majority had flipped to foreign, mostly German-speaking guests; the 1961 bombing campaign cut Italian arrivals by a quarter in a single year (notes 06, §1, [V/D])

Bolzano passed 1 million overnight stays for the first time in 2025 (1,042,903), up 81% since 2010; per inhabitant it is still lightly touristed, about 8 nights against 67 for the province (notes 06, §2, [V/D])

Official tourism channels no longer hide the fascist layer, but the sales copy folds the fascist city into a harmony-of-cultures narrative ('armonia di stili', 'Stadt der Gegensätze', 'alpin und mediterran') (notes 06, §4, [V] and [INF])
No published work applies 'translocality' to Bolzano or South Tyrol: 'a genuine gap the studio can occupy' (notes 06, §5)
Tags used: [V] read in the primary document, [S] secondary article fetched in full, [SS] search snippet only, [D] derived from the downloaded data, [INF] inference (notes 06, header)

entries.title: One Monument, One Town, Two Ideologies: The Monument to the Victory of Bolzano-Bozen
text: Malcolm Angelucci and Stefano Kerschbamer read the exhibition inside the Monument to Victory as a piece of text and design. They find its history “monologic”: it casts the visitor as a “good historian” and leaves one correct reading.

Of the red LED ring on the column they write that it resembles “the ‘open’ sign of a cheap restaurant”. The monument is “once again ‘open for business’, but business of a different order”. The file is the journal's full text, saved as a web page.
facts: Malcolm Angelucci and Stefano Kerschbamer, Public History Review 24 (2017): 54–75, doi:10.5130/phrj.v24i0.5776 (notes 06, §5 item 10, [V]; file)
A textual and design analysis of BZ '18-'45 that criticises its 'monologic' objective history and its construction of the visitor (notes 06, §5 item 10, [V])

The exhibition constructs the visitor as a 'good historian'; the red LED ring resembles 'the 'open' sign of a cheap restaurant', so the monument is 'once again 'open for business', but business of a different order' (notes 06, §4, [V])
Cited in the notes among the academic literature that treats Bolzano as a public-history model, with critiques of its didactic, 'correct reading' design (notes 06, §4)
The server returned an HTML full text instead of a PDF; the file is that saved full text (manifest)

entries.title: Südtirol Toolbox / Bildstil
text: The image rules of the Südtirol umbrella brand, issued by the province's marketing agency IDM in 2019. Pictures are to move “weg von ‚Postkartenmotiven‘ hin zu mehr Echtheit, Natürlichkeit und Authentizität”.
The brand's core is restated as a “kontrastreiche Symbiose aus alpin und mediterran”. This research reads that phrase as the border position turned into a selling point.
facts: 'Südtirol Toolbox / Bildstil', the image-style rules of the umbrella brand Dachmarke Südtirol, © IDM 2019, 31 pages (manifest; file)

The umbrella brand addresses people interested in 'Nachhaltigkeit, Aktivität, Natur und Originalität'; imagery should move 'weg von „Postkartenmotiven“ hin zu mehr Echtheit, Natürlichkeit und Authentizität' (notes 06, §1, [V])
The rules restate the 2005 brand core, the 'kontrastreiche Symbiose aus alpin und mediterran, Spontaneität und Verlässlichkeit, Natur und Kultur' (notes 06, §1, [V]; file)
The notes read 'alpin und mediterran' as a statement of in-betweenness that markets the border position, useful for a translocality framing (notes 06, §1, [INF])
Rights: copyright IDM Südtirol; for research use only (manifest)

entries.title: Fascist Monumentality in Bolzano and Trieste: Can Public History Help to Deal with it?
text: Iris Pupella-Noguès compares how Bolzano and Trieste deal with their fascist buildings. Bolzano's municipal brochure of 2007 lists 28 monuments and buildings and is openly historical. Trieste's brochure of the same year mentions fascism three times.

The chapter also covers the documentation centre in the Monument to Victory, which grew out of a petition by three historians in 2011, and the Hannah Arendt sentence hung across the Piffrader relief on 5 November 2017.
facts: Iris Pupella-Noguès, chapter in Knowledgescape: Insights on Public Humanities (ed. Burgio, Fischer, Sartor), Edizioni Ca' Foscari, Filologie medievali e moderne 25, 2021, pp. 65–84, doi:10.30687/978-88-6969-542-1/004 (notes 06, §5 item 11, [V]; file)
Covers the Bolzano 2007 tour brochure 'Percorso tra architettura e fascismo', BZ '18-'45 and the Piffrader relief (manifest)

The 2007 municipal brochure lists 28 monuments and buildings and is explicitly historical; Trieste's 2007 brochure 'Itinerario dell'architettura razionalista' mentions fascism only three times (notes 06, §4, [V])

BZ '18-'45 arose from a petition by the historians Andrea Di Michele, Hans Heiss and Hannes Obermair in early 2011 and won a Special Commendation at the European Museum of the Year Award 2016 (notes 06, §4, [V])

The Piffrader relief on the former Casa del Fascio was covered on 5 Nov 2017 with Hannah Arendt's 'No one has the right to obey' in German, Italian and Ladin, a work by Arnold Holzknecht and Michele Bernardi (notes 06, §4, [V])
In 2009 Landeshauptmann Durnwalder said the relief and the Alpini monument 'do not have any justifications anymore' (notes 06, §4, [V])
Rights: CC BY 4.0 (manifest); the file states 'Creative Commons 4.0 Attribution alone' (file)

entries.title: Tourismusentwicklung in Südtirol: Utopische, faschistische Architektur: Tourismus als strategische Investition in Südtirol
text: A two-page description of a doctoral project by Catrina Klee at the University of Lucerne. Its hypothesis: fascist political and military infrastructure is “the basis for turning South Tyrol into a region dominated by car and sports tourism between the 1920s and the 1940s”, and tourism projects “acted as accelerators of the Italianization”.
These are hypotheses, not findings. It is the closest work this research found to its own question. Nothing yet compares the regime's tourism posters with post-war campaigns.
facts: Two-page PhD project description by Catrina Klee, Graduate School of Humanities and Social Sciences, University of Lucerne; supervisor Valentin Groebner; the title is the project's (file; manifest)

Hypothesis: fascist political and military infrastructure investments 'are the basis for turning South Tyrol into a region dominated by car and sports tourism between the 1920s and the 1940s' (notes 06, §1, [V])
Tourism projects 'acted as accelerators of the Italianization'; the unrealized 'utopias … shape and preformat the later change from the 1950s onward' (notes 06, §1, [V])
Identifies a shift from spa tourism (Bolzano, Merano) to active summer and sports tourism after WWI (notes 06, §1, [V])
The closest work the notes found: no scholarship directly compares fascist-era ENIT/EPT poster imagery with postwar campaigns (notes 06, §1)
Rights: author's copyright, publicly posted by Univ. Lucerne, for research use only (manifest)

entries.title: Dekret des Landeshauptmanns vom 26. September 2022, Nr. 25: Kriterien und Modalitäten für die Erhebung, die Festsetzung der Obergrenze und die Zuweisung von Gästebetten
text: The provincial regulation that caps guest beds in South Tyrol. The cap is the sum of all lawful sleeping places for guests over 14, in hotels, private rentals and farm holidays, with a quota for the province and one for each municipality. The Landtag voted it in July 2022 on the basis of the 2019 stock.
Beds went on rising all the same: 233,847 in 2022, 262,869 in 2025. The text held is the consolidated version as of 22 October 2026.
facts: The regulation on the guest-bed cap, published in the Amtsblatt (BUR) of 29 Sep 2022, Nr. 39; consolidated text as of 2026-10-22, saved as HTML because lexbrowser offers PDF export only through JavaScript (manifest)

Legal basis: Art. 34 and 38 of LG 10 July 2018, Nr. 9 'Raum und Landschaft'; Art. 1 defines the cap as the sum of all lawful sleeping places for guests over 14, covering hotels (LG 58/1988), private room and holiday-flat rentals (LG 12/1995) and farm holidays (LG 7/2008) (notes 06, §2, [V])
Art. 6 sets provincial and municipal bed quotas by category; released beds are credited 95% to the municipal and 5% to the provincial quota (notes 06, §2, [V])

The Landtag voted the cap on 21 July 2022, based on the 2019 stock plus rights acquired since; the regulation was approved on 13 Sep 2022 (notes 06, §2, [V]); the number of the 2022 law itself was not identified (manifest)
Despite the cap, provincial beds rose from 233,847 (2022) to 262,869 (2025) (notes 06, §2, [V/D])
Amended by DLH 29 Mar 2023, Nr. 9 (not held), DLH 13 Apr 2026, Nr. 10 and DLH 23 Sep 2026, Nr. 28 (rows 6.11, 6.18) (notes 06, §2, [V])

A petition by the Heimatpflegeverband and the Dachverband für Natur- und Umweltschutz (Jan 2026, about 11,000 signatures) defends the 'Bettenstoppverordnung vom 13. September 2022': 'Tourismus in Maßen statt in Massen' (notes 06, §2, [V])

entries.title: ASTAT, arrivals, overnight stays and beds by municipality, 2023
text: Arrivals, overnight stays and beds for each of the 116 municipalities of South Tyrol in 2023, from the provincial statistics office.

Bolzano had more arrivals than any other municipality (388,743) and ranked only tenth by nights (870,822). Visitors stay 2.24 nights on average, against 4.95 in Kastelruth. Per inhabitant that makes about 8 nights a year, where the province as a whole counts 67.

Fields: FN_BETTEN beds, FN_ANK arrivals, FN_NACHT nights, FN_NACHTSO/WI summer/winter nights, FN_NACHTIN/AU Italian/foreign nights, FN_BETTLAS bed occupancy % (manifest)

Bolzano's average stay was 2.24 nights against 4.95 in Kastelruth; its bed occupancy was 47.22% (notes 06, §2, [V/D])
2023 nights per inhabitant: Bolzano 8.17, province 67.3 (notes 06, §2, [D])

entries.title: Dekret des Landeshauptmanns vom 13. April 2026, Nr. 10: Änderung der Verordnung über die Kriterien und Modalitäten für die Erhebung, die Festsetzung der Obergrenze und die Zuweisung von Gästebetten
text: An amendment to the bed cap. In municipalities at risk of depopulation it extends acquired building rights in tourism zones from four to nine years. Municipalities with more than 500,000 nights in 2025 are excluded, and so is Bolzano.

Beds for private tourist rentals go first to people who let at their own residence, and no allocation may take anyone above two rental units. This research reads it as the first provincial rule aimed squarely at professional short-term letting.
facts: Amendment to the bed-cap regulation DLH 25/2022 (row 6.05), published in the Amtsblatt (BUR) of 16 Apr 2026, Nr. 16 (manifest; file)

In municipalities at risk of depopulation or structurally weak (Table A) it extends acquired rights in tourism zones from 4 to 9 years; municipalities with more than 500,000 nights in 2025 are excluded, which excludes Bolzano (notes 06, §2, [V])

The extension needs a council vote per zone weighing water, energy, traffic and staff housing, a sustainability certification within 2 years for new establishments, and the 150-bed maximum (notes 06, §2, [V])
Beds for private tourist rentals go preferably to applicants who rent at their own residence or registered seat; no allocation may bring a person above two rental units (notes 06, §2, [V])
Kompatscher: 'Die Regelung über die Bettenobergrenze bleibt'; Walcher: 'bleibt die Gemeinde untätig, verfällt die Zone' (notes 06, §2, [V], stol.it 2 Apr 2026)
The notes read it as the first provincial instrument aimed squarely at Airbnb-type professionalisation (notes 06, §2, [INF])

text: Arrivals and overnight stays for the province and every municipality from 1950 to 2025, by kind of establishment and by origin. The table shown is an extract for the province and for Bolzano.

entries.title: Ain't no mountain nice enough: UNESCO listing of the Dolomites and tourism demand
text: A Banca d'Italia occasional paper on what the 2009 UNESCO listing of the Dolomites did to tourism. Across 349 municipalities, demand rose by an average of 9.1 per cent over the five years after the listing, most clearly among Italian visitors. The number of establishments did not grow and beds fell.
The manifest and notes cite the paper under its Italian title, “Vette senza eguali”. The file held is the English version.
facts: Michele Cascarano, Carlo Fezzi and Nicolas Javier Rodriguez, Banca d'Italia, Questioni di Economia e Finanza (Occasional Papers) no. 1027, June 2026, doi:10.32057/0.QEF.2026.1027 (file)

The manifest and notes give the Italian title 'Vette senza eguali: il riconoscimento UNESCO delle Dolomiti e la domanda turistica'; the held PDF is the English paper with the title above (manifest; file)

After the 2009 listing, Dolomite municipalities in the provinces of Trento, Bolzano and Belluno, 'soprattutto quelli del Trentino', recorded more tourist presences, more markedly among Italian visitors (notes 06, §1, [V])

Establishments did not grow and beds fell, which the authors read as a shift towards smaller, plausibly higher-quality establishments; growth brought no more land consumption or waste (notes 06, §1, [V])
Abstract: 349 municipalities, 2005–2013; an average increase in tourism demand of 9.1 per cent over the five years after the listing (file, abstract)
Filed in the notes under the marketing effect of the UNESCO listing (notes 06, §1)

entries.title: Inside Airbnb, Trentino listings, scrape of 28 September 2026
text: Inside Airbnb's scrape of 28 September 2026, 10,237 listings. Despite the region's name in its title it covers the Province of Trento only. No listing lies inside Bolzano, and Inside Airbnb publishes nothing for South Tyrol, so this file serves as a comparison and no more.
For Bolzano the research has one commercial estimate, 244 active listings, whose method is not disclosed.
facts: Inside Airbnb's 'Trentino, Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol' scrape of 28 Sep 2026: a listings summary of 10,237 listings and a neighbourhoods file (manifest; file)
It covers only the Province of Trento: maximum latitude 46.49, none inside a Bolzano bounding box; Inside Airbnb has no South Tyrol or Bolzano dataset (manifest; notes 06, §2, [V/D])
